nodes.title: Cloud fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Every cloud certification starts with the same vocabulary: IaaS / PaaS / SaaS, public / private / hybrid, capex vs opex, elasticity, regions and AZs. Getting these right is half the foundational exam.

flashcards.front: IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS — pick an example of each.
flashcards.back: IaaS (Infrastructure): EC2, Azure VM, Compute Engine — you manage OS and up. PaaS (Platform): App Engine, Elastic Beanstalk, App Service — you manage code, provider manages runtime. SaaS (Software): Gmail, Salesforce — you just use it. As you go up the stack, you get convenience, lose control.

flashcards.front: Region vs Availability Zone — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: A region is a geographic area (us-east-1, europe-west2). An AZ is one or more data centers inside a region with independent power/cooling/network. AZs in a region are connected by low-latency fiber but isolated from each other's failures. Best practice: spread workload across 2-3 AZs for HA.

Scalability: the system can be grown (add capacity to handle 10x load). Elasticity: it auto-shrinks back when load drops — you don't pay for idle capacity. A scalable system isn't necessarily elastic (a manually-resized DB is scalable but not elastic). Cloud's killer feature is being both.

flashcards.front: Capex vs opex — why does cloud favor opex?
flashcards.back: Capex (capital expenditure): big upfront purchase (a server, a building). Opex (operating expenditure): ongoing per-unit cost (cloud usage, electricity). Cloud turns infrastructure into opex — no $500k server purchases, just monthly bills. Easier for finance to scale, easier to abandon a project without sunk cost.

pairs.stem: An organization wants its email, file storage, and collaboration tools to be fully managed by the provider, with no servers to install or patch. Which cloud service model fits this requirement?
A startup wants to avoid large upfront hardware purchases and instead pay only for the IT capacity it actually consumes each month. Which financial model best describes this approach?
In Microsoft 365's shared responsibility model for SaaS, which task remains the customer's responsibility?
pairs.option: Maintaining the physical network hardware in Microsoft regions

pairs.stem: A marketing team wants to build a simple low-code app to track event registrations without writing custom backend code. Which component of the Power Platform should they use?

A retailer experiences holiday traffic that is 10x higher than normal. They want services to automatically add capacity during peak hours and shrink afterward. Which cloud characteristic provides this behavior?

A regulated bank wants to keep some workloads on-premises for compliance reasons while running other workloads in the public cloud, with both connected through secure networking. Which deployment model best describes this configuration?

nodes.title: Compliance frameworks: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Compliance is the discipline of mapping your controls to an external framework (PCI, HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001) and proving it to an auditor. Most exam questions test which framework owns which scope, not the minutiae of each clause.

flashcards.back: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard. Applies to anyone who stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data (PAN, expiry, CVV). 12 high-level requirements: firewalls, no defaults, encrypted storage, encrypted transmission, antivirus, secure dev, restrict access, MFA, log, test, policy. Required by Visa/Mastercard, not by law.

flashcards.front: HIPAA vs HITRUST — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: HIPAA is U.S. law for protected health information (PHI) — sets the legal requirements but is high-level on technical controls. HITRUST CSF is a certifiable framework that operationalizes HIPAA (plus ISO, NIST, PCI) into specific testable controls. Healthcare orgs are legally HIPAA-bound; many also pursue HITRUST cert to prove diligence.

American Institute of CPAs report on a SaaS company's controls across five trust criteria: security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, privacy. Type I = controls designed at a point in time. Type II = controls operated effectively over 6-12 months. Enterprise customers ask for the Type II as proof you're not making it up.

flashcards.front: GDPR — what does it require beyond US-style privacy laws?
flashcards.back: European General Data Protection Regulation. Requires explicit consent (not pre-ticked), right to access / deletion / portability, 72-hour breach notification, data protection officer (for large processors), data minimization, and Privacy Impact Assessments for high-risk processing. Fines: up to 4% of global revenue. Applies to anyone processing EU residents' data, regardless of company location.

pairs.stem: Lawyers need to place certain mailboxes and SharePoint sites on legal hold and search across them for case-related content. Which Microsoft Purview feature is designed for this workflow?
Two business divisions inside the same tenant must be prevented from communicating in Teams to avoid conflicts of interest. Which Microsoft Purview feature enforces this segregation?
Which Microsoft 365 feature lets administrators automatically delete user mailboxes and SharePoint content after a defined retention period to meet records management policies?

A company must prevent users from emailing files containing credit card numbers to external recipients. Which Microsoft Purview capability enforces this rule across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams?

An information protection team wants to apply labels such as 'Confidential' or 'Public' to Word documents so encryption and watermarks are automatically enforced when the file is shared. Which Microsoft Purview feature provides this?
An organization wants HR managers to be alerted when employees download abnormally large amounts of data shortly before resigning. Which Microsoft Purview solution targets this scenario?

nodes.title: Licensing: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Licensing. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An organization with 200 employees needs Microsoft 365 desktop apps, Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, and Intune device management at a low per-user price. Which plan is the most cost-effective fit?
flashcards.back: Microsoft 365 Business Premium is targeted at organizations up to 300 seats and bundles Office desktop apps, Exchange/Teams/SharePoint, Intune, and Defender for Business — typically the most cost-effective for SMBs.

flashcards.front: Which Microsoft 365 Enterprise plan is required to obtain Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium), Power BI Pro, and Teams Phone all in a single license?
flashcards.back: Microsoft 365 E5 is the top enterprise SKU and bundles advanced security (Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, Defender for Identity), Purview Premium, Power BI Pro, and Teams Phone.

flashcards.front: A retailer wants licenses for warehouse and store staff who only need email, web/mobile Office apps, and basic Teams chat — they share kiosks and don't need full desktop Office. Which plan family is designed for this audience?
flashcards.back: Microsoft 365 F1 and F3 are the frontline worker SKUs, priced for shift workers who primarily use shared devices and need essential collaboration without full desktop Office.

flashcards.front: Which statement most accurately describes the difference between Microsoft 365 E3 and Office 365 E3?
flashcards.back: Microsoft 365 plans bundle Office 365 + Windows Enterprise + Enterprise Mobility + Security (EMS). Office 365 plans contain only the Office 365 productivity stack. Enterprise Mobility + Security E3, and Office 365 E3 in one bundle

pairs.stem: A retailer wants licenses for warehouse and store staff who only need email, web/mobile Office apps, and basic Teams chat — they share kiosks and don't need full desktop Office. Which plan family is designed for this audience?
Which statement most accurately describes the difference between Microsoft 365 E3 and Office 365 E3?
pairs.option: Microsoft 365 E3 is per device while Office 365 E3 is per user

pairs.stem: Which combination of capabilities is the primary differentiator of Microsoft 365 E5 over Microsoft 365 E3?

An organization with 200 employees needs Microsoft 365 desktop apps, Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, and Intune device management at a low per-user price. Which plan is the most cost-effective fit?
Which Microsoft 365 Enterprise plan is required to obtain Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium), Power BI Pro, and Teams Phone all in a single license?

A customer wants to lower their per-month cost on Microsoft 365 E3 and is willing to commit for 12 months instead of paying month-to-month. Which billing option provides a discount in exchange for that commitment?

pairs.stem: An IT manager wants only managed corporate phones that are enrolled and compliant to access Microsoft 365 mail. Which Microsoft service enforces device enrollment and compliance policies?
An admin wants a numeric measurement of the Microsoft 365 tenant's security posture and recommended actions to improve it. Which Microsoft service provides this score?
An admin wants real-time information about ongoing service incidents affecting their Microsoft 365 tenant (for example, an Outlook on the web outage). Which tool should they consult?
Microsoft publishes uptime commitments for Microsoft 365 services. What is the financially backed uptime SLA for most Microsoft 365 services such as Exchange Online and SharePoint Online?
Where should an admin look for upcoming Microsoft 365 features that are in preview, rolling out, or recently launched, with target dates and categories?
A project team wants a single workspace that combines persistent chat, file sharing, video meetings, and tabs for third-party apps. Which Microsoft 365 service best meets this need?
